clinical_category: Halo brace safety - pin-site infection and loosening surveillance
blueprint_topic: Prevention and early recognition of complications from halo skeletal fixation
stem: A nurse cares for a client wearing a halo brace after a cervical spine injury. Which nursing action is appropriate?

options.A: Perform prescribed pin-site care and assess regularly for drainage, erythema, tenderness, or evidence of pin or ring loosening
options.B: Leave the pin sites unassessed because infection and loosening are not recognized halo complications
options.C: Independently retighten any loose halo pin without the trained spine clinician's assessment
options.D: Remove a painful or draining pin at the bedside without an order or replacement plan

rationale: A is correct. Current NCBI/StatPearls guidance identifies pin-site infection and pin or halo-ring loosening among recognized halo complications and describes ongoing pin-site care and follow-up checks as part of halo management. Nursing surveillance therefore includes inspection for local inflammatory or drainage findings and for loss of fixation integrity, with concerning findings escalated to the spine team. B ignores recognized complications. C and D exceed the nursing role and may jeopardize cervical immobilization; pin tightening or replacement is performed according to the halo protocol by appropriately trained clinicians. The final item intentionally does not prescribe one universal cleansing solution, frequency, or torque value because those details vary by protocol and patient factors.
educational_objective: Maintain halo safety through protocol-directed pin-site care and surveillance for infection or loosening, and escalate fixation concerns rather than independently manipulating or removing halo pins.
source_version_date: Current StatPearls/NCBI Bookshelf edition available in 2026; accessed 2026-08-18
source_locator: NCBI Bookshelf 'Halo Brace' → post-application care: ongoing pin-site care and follow-up checks are used to reduce complications. Complications: pin-site infection and pin/halo-ring loosening are recognized complications; persistent drainage/infection may require clinician-directed treatment or pin replacement. Enhancing Healthcare Team Outcomes: trained nursing staff provide ordered pin-site care and monitor for complications, with medical consultation when infection is suspected.
source_claim_supported: Current NCBI/StatPearls guidance directly supports ongoing halo pin-site care and surveillance for pin-site infection and loosening, while reserving corrective fixation procedures for appropriately trained clinicians.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control client-needs subcategory (10–16% of items); this item tests prevention and recognition of infection and mechanical complications associated with an immobilization device.
correction_summary: Substantive evidence rebuild. The generic AANN source was replaced with current NCBI/StatPearls halo guidance. The final item keeps the infection/loosening surveillance construct but removes a universal cleaning regimen, cleansing agent, and torque schedule from the keyed answer because those details are protocol-dependent.
audit_findings: The original generic AANN URL did not provide the strongest current exact locator for halo pin-site care.
Current NCBI/StatPearls directly recognizes pin-site infection and fixation loosening as important halo complications and supports ongoing pin-site care and surveillance.
The final item avoids universal cleansing-solution, cleaning-frequency, and torque prescriptions that may vary by protocol.
Independent pin manipulation or removal was excluded because it may compromise cervical immobilization and is not the nursing action supported by the source.
Independent adversarial second pass found one uniquely correct answer, no unsupported numeric or cleansing precision, no second defensible option, no cueing, and no unresolved conflict.
